page: Microsoft Azure M16ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores running at 2.7 GHz. The processor includes a 38 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AVX512F, and AES instructions. The instance is equipped with 438.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 27.34 GB per core, alongside 524 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance at 1038.48 and Geekbench single-core score at 878.0, fall into the bottom 10% tier. Similarly, single-threaded operations like gzip compression at 17.26 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 6.68 GB/sec are poor. However, multi-core and memory-bound benchmarks perform in the average range. The instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 10944.09, a Passmark CPU score of 11764.97, and a Redis SET throughput of 10.46 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 73.69 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations.

The primary tradeoff of the M16ms is its modest single-threaded CPU speed relative to its massive memory footprint. While it is not suited for compute-heavy single-threaded tasks or medium-to-large LLM inference, its high resource density makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier CPU performance. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise database operations, and memory-intensive data processing tasks where RAM capacity is the primary bottleneck.
